transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-15
Start time: 15:00 EDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Mark Daniels (Head of Cloud Ops, PioneerTrust), Elena Ruiz (CISO), Amit Patel (Lead Backend Engineer)

Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
PioneerTrust is evaluating Redwood for a mix of hosted and private deployment options. Primary concerns are strict US-only data residency for banking data, audit logging restrictions, retention limits, and evidence for SOC2/HIPAA (for certain product lines). Conversation covered Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs, KMS/HSM integration, log redaction and retention, network connectivity (VPC peering vs private link), and a proposed pilot and benchmark window. Next steps: Redwood to send SOC2 + security docs; schedule SE-led deep dive and perf tests.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, I'm an AE, with Priya our SE. hows everybody doing?
[00:05] Mark: Good, thanks. we had a quick last minute sync but all good.
[00:08] Elena: Hi, Elena here. hope this is recorded.
[00:10] Jordan: yes recorded. quick agenda, we want to understand your requirements for data residency and compliance, run through deployment models (hosted/dedicated/private), and see if we should plan a technical deep dive. sound good?
[00:20] Amit: yeah sounds fine. quick context: PioneerTrust has retail banking in the US and a small EU payments team. for the retail stuff we need strict US-only residency and GLBA/FFIEC alignment. the EU team has GDPR constraints for personal data, less urgent today but part of overall reqs.
[00:36] Priya: thanks, that's helpful. can you confirm if the use case is PII in prompts/responses or analytics only?
[00:42] Mark: primarily PII in prompts — customer support transcripts, account details, some KYC snippets. we also plan embeddings for search that may include hashed identifiers.
[00:50] Elena: also, we have internal policy that raw logs of prompts cannot leave our VPC; auditors have flagged third-party log retention as a risk.
[00:58] Jordan: understood. Priya, do you want to run through how Redwood handles hosting options?
[01:02] Priya: sure. at a high level we offer hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and a private deployment option. hosted is fastest to get started — it's multitenant but we provide contractual controls, SOC 2, data processing agreements, and region scoping in many cases. dedicated gives you isolated pools and better predictable throughput. private is our VPC/on-prem control plane where the customer manages networking and we can deploy into your VPC or even air-gapped on prem if required.
[01:25] Mark: for us, the ask is US-only for retail data and EU-only for the EU teams. can hosted guarantee that?
[01:31] Priya: hosted can be constrained to regions — we can guarantee that data is processed in our US region for a customer, but for the highest assurance customers often choose Dedicated or Private because they want network-level isolation and control over logs.
[01:42] Elena: what about logs — call payloads, request traces, and model prompts — do you ever keep those? our policy is that third-party vendors can store telemetry but not raw prompts, and retention must be <30 days unless approved.
[01:54] Jordan: we have options. by default we retain telemetry for X days for debugging, but for enterprise contracts we can configure log redaction, reduced retention, and route logs to the customer's KMS/archival. Priya?
[02:03] Priya: yes. for Dedicated and Private, logs and traces can be pushed to your logging endpoint; we also support zero retention mode for prompts where we don't persist raw prompt text in our control plane. there are tradeoffs for debugging — no retention can make root cause analysis harder, but it's common for banks. also we support field-level redaction and PII tokenization before it's stored.
[02:21] Amit: how does the KMS integration work? we need to use our AWS KMS for encryption keys and HSM-backed keys for certain operations.
[02:27] Priya: we support customer-managed keys (CMK) on Dedicated and Private. for hosted, we offer an encrypted-in-transit and at-rest model with our KMS but we can integrate to your KMS via BYOK for some enterprise plans, or use a customer HSM for Private deployments.
[02:41] Elena: auditors will also ask for proof of GC or HSM usage. do you provide attestations?
[02:46] Jordan: yes, we share SOC 2 Type II reports, and for certain customers we can provide additional attestation language. I'll send over the security whitepaper and our SOC report after this call.
[02:56] Mark: great. latency is also a concern; if we move to Private, what's the perf hit compared to hosted?
[03:01] Priya: Private running in your VPC typically has slightly higher overhead because of network egress rules and KMS calls, but it's minimal if you colocate GPUs. Dedicated with our reserved pools in the same region can give you the best latency/throughput balance without giving up isolation. we also have smart routing and KV cache to improve token-level latency and reduce cost.
[03:22] Amit: you mentioned KV cash earlier — you mean KV cache?
[03:24] Priya: yes kv cache, sorry the auto transcript sometimes does that.
[03:27] Elena: compliance with GDPR — can you ensure that EU personal data doesn't get replicated to US for backups or profiling?
[03:33] Priya: for Private deployments in EU we can keep everything in-region. for hosted we offer region-scoped processing and we can commit to no cross-border replication in contract language and technical controls. backups can be configured to be region-local as well.
[03:45] Mark: what about model fine-tuning — are we allowed to fine-tune on customer data? cross-border implications there too.
[03:50] Jordan: fine-tuning on customer data is blocked by default in hosted. we only do fine-tuning under explicit customer agreement and typically in Dedicated/Private where the customer controls the training data location.
[03:59] Amit: auditors ask for an audit trail of access to the model and data — who touched what and when. can we get immutable audit logs?
[04:06] Priya: yes, we emit audit logs for admin actions, model deploys, and access. for Private, you can push these logs to your SIEM directly. we can also sign logs and provide tamper-evidence depending on the compliance program.
[04:19] Elena: retention windows — do you have built-in controls? we need ability to set per-asset retention, and automatic purge for PII.
[04:26] Priya: we have retention policies you can configure per-asset type. automatic PII purge is supported via a configurable policy engine in Dedicated and Private.
[04:34] Jordan: quick question on timeline — what's your expected timeframe to make a decision?
[04:37] Mark: we'd like to run a pilot in Q2, ideally late April/May. need security sign-off before we start.
[04:44] Jordan: perfect, we can run a 2-week benchmark with a dedicated pool or a private eval deployment. Priya, I'd recommend the dedicated perf run first to compare latency/cost, then a private POC if they need the VPC controls.
[04:56] Priya: yeah i agree — start with dedicated reserved pool in our US region with KV cache enabled, run our standard throughput and latency suite, then if they need us to deploy in their VPC we can schedule that as follow-up.
[05:06] Amit: okay, for the bench we'll need 99th percentile latency numbers, token throughput, and cost per 1k tokens. and we need to validate that logs aren't leaving our account.
[05:15] Priya: we'll provide those metrics and a benchmarking spreadsheet. we also do a small-scale warmup test to account for cache warming.
[05:22] Mark: security team will want to review network diagrams, data flows, and who has access to keys.
[05:28] Elena: also, encryption in transit — TLS is fine, but we need mTLS for internal endpoints. do you support mutual TLS?
[05:34] Priya: yes, Private supports mTLS for internal endpoints and we can configure mutual auth for the logging endpoint.
[05:41] Jordan: any other blockers?
[05:43] Elena: procurement — also need contract language for subprocessor lists and data processing addendum.
[05:48] Jordan: we have a standard DPA and subprocessors list; I'll include them in the follow up.
[05:52] Amit: one more — we have an internal rule that no raw prompts are persisted outside our region, and embeddings must be hashed. doable?
[05:58] Priya: yes, for Dedicated/Private we can hash embeddings client-side, and configure zero prompt retention or prompt redaction. for hosted, we'll need the DPA and contractual controls but we can scope processing to US.
[06:10] Mark: pricing — dedicated and private are more expensive. what cost factors should we expect?
[06:15] Jordan: main cost drivers are reserved GPU capacity, data egress (if using cross-region), KMS request volume for external CMK, and retention costs if you want long audit retention. we can provide a cost model based on your expected QPS and average tokens per request.
[06:30] Elena: what about fallbacks — if a dedicated pool is saturated do you failover to hosted and risk cross-region data movement?
[06:36] Priya: we have routing policies. by default you can configure strict routing (no cross-fallback) or allow fallback to a compatible model variant in the same region. for sensitive workloads we recommend strict no-fallback.
[06:48] Mark: ok that helps.
[06:50] Jordan: quick recap and next steps — i'll send SOC2 + security whitepaper and subprocessors list; Priya will schedule an SE deep-dive and send benchmarking template; Amit will share data residency checklist and sample flows. we agreed on a pilot in late April/May pending security review.
[07:07] Elena: thanks. can you also include a sample contract clause for data residency?
[07:11] Jordan: yes, i'll include a clause template.
[07:14] Priya: i'll follow up on the perf numbers and sample network diagrams.
[07:18] Mark: great, thanks everyone.
[07:20] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up end of day tomorrow with the docs.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional transcription errors (kv cash -> kv cache), speaker overlaps, and some redaction-sensitive fragments left vague per recording.
